items.item:
6. Two accepted changes in turn write entries numbered n and n + 1, and the
   audit sequence (M12) holds n + 1 after the second; two concurrent changes
   take two distinct consecutive numbers, and the one whose transaction
   committed first holds the lower.
   Shows A15-1. [witness: verification:registry_a15_sequential_and_concurrent_changes_number_in_order]
statements:
```text
for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence   -- A15-1
erase(d) accepted => no entry with instant < start_of(d) remains   -- A15-2
erase(d) accepted => its erasure entry e has e.instant >= start_of(d)   -- A15-3
```

verdicts.why: The selected test asserts sequential and concurrent changes receive distinct consecutive sequence numbers, updates M12, and relates the lower number to the inferred application/commit order. It does not assert that erasure leaves no entry before the cutoff or that each erasure entry's instant is at or after the cutoff, so A15-2 and A15-3 are unasserted.
